programme.title: New Zealand: Earth's Mythical Islands
programme.desc: Isolated since the time of the dinosaurs, New Zealand's wildlife has been left to its own devices, with surprising consequences. Its ancient forests are still stalked by predators from the Jurassic era. It's also one of the most geologically active countries on earth. From Kiwis with their giant eggs, to forest-dwelling penguins and helicopter-riding sheep dogs, meet the astonishing creatures and resilient people who must rise to the challenges of their beautiful, dramatic and demanding home.

programme.title: Secrets of Bones
programme.desc: Ben Garrod delves into the surprising ways in which bone has evolved to help vertebrates sense the world around them. He reveals why predators like the wolf have eyes at the front of their skull, whereas prey animals such as sheep usually have eye sockets on the sides of their heads. He finds out how the skull of the great grey owl has helped it develop such extraordinary hearing and uncovers the secret behind one bizarre creature's uniquely flexible nose.

programme.title: Timothy Spall: Back at Sea
programme.desc: As summer comes to a close, Timothy Spall's trip around the coast of his beloved Britain reaches the halfway mark. He encounters several Scottish ports and islands, mostly in the famous Scottish misty drizzle. Before the weather worsens, he winds his way through the Scottish western islands and takes his barge Princess Matilda back to her roots by venturing up the Caledonian Canal, a shortcut from the west of Scotland to the east, which sets up next year's trip down the east coast and back home to London. This year, Timothy and his wife Shane have travelled further than in any other of their previous six years at sea. All they need is somewhere to moor up for winter.

programme.title: The Lost City of Sanxingdui
programme.desc: In the mountains of Sichuan, China, lies a mysterious ancient city that was consigned to oblivion until the chance discovery of a jade object in 1927. Since that first find, over 10,000 artefacts made of gold, jade, ivory and bronze have been unearthed, buried by the inhabitants in sacrificial pits before they left the city about 3,000 years ago. The finds include objects unlike any other: curiously shaped bronze heads and masks covered in gold foil. The scale of the site and the number of treasures make Sanxingdui one of the most important archaeological discoveries of our time. Was this city once the capital of the ancient Shu kingdom – a kingdom whose very existence was doubted by some? At Sanxingdui, Bronze Age treasures speak to our imagination and open a new chapter of history.

programme.title: The Planets
programme.desc: The rocky planets Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars were born at the same time from the same material, yet they have lived radically different lives. What immense forces are at play?

programme.title: Remembers...
programme.desc: Dame Janet Suzman shares her memories of making The Singing Detective, the groundbreaking Dennis Potter drama which is widely regarded as a landmark television moment. Praising Potter's remarkable writing, Janet describes the electric feeling on set for the cast, led by Michael Gambon, as they understood they were dealing with something truly special. She describes how each actor fully committed to their roles in order to bring this visionary, multi-layered piece of drama to life.

programme.title: The Singing Detective
programme.desc: Dennis Potter's classic drama serial with music. Pulp thriller writer Philip Marlow is in hospital with the skin complaint psoriasis, tormented by his past and threatened by his future. His memories, his 1930s-style gumshoe fiction and his disease weave him an altered reality.

programme.title: The Singing Detective
programme.desc: Marlow faces his personal misery of the talking cure with the psychologist who wants to help him with his psychosomatic psoriasis and has actually read Marlow's novel. Nicola, an ambitious and demanding actress, appears in Marlow's hospital ward just as he is thinking about her. Marlow is suspicious of his former wife, and his wretched state exposes his vulnerability. Only the fact that his imagination is running riot keeps him occupied.

programme.desc: Ben Garrod uncovers the secrets of how vertebrates capture and devour their food using extreme jaws, bizarre teeth and specialised bony tools. programme.title: Ancient Worlds
programme.desc: In Richard Miles's epic story of civilization, there have been plenty of examples of the great men of history, but none came close to the legend of Alexander of Macedon, known to us as 'the Great'. Uniting the fractious Greek city-states, he led them on a crusade against the old enemy, Persia, and in little more than a decade created an empire that stretched from Egypt in the west to Afghanistan in the east. But it was Alexander's successors, the Hellenistic Kings, who had to make sense of the legacy of this charismatic adventurer. By knuckling down to the hard graft of politics, taxation and public works, they created something far more enduring than a mere legend - they built a civilization. Richard traces Alexander's battle-scarred route through Turkey, Syria and Lebanon to Egypt and ultimately to the western Punjab, Pakistan, where he discovers fascinating traces of a city where Greek west and Buddhist east were united in an intriguing new way.

programme.desc: A foot-stomping return to the BBC vaults of Top of the Pops, The Old Grey Whistle Test and Later with Jools as the programme spins itself to a time when disco ruled the floor, the airwaves and our minds. The visual floorfillers include classics from luminaries such as Chic, Labelle and Rose Royce to glitter ball surprises by The Village People.

programme.title: TOTP2
programme.desc: Mark Radcliffe introduces this archive tribute to the Queen of Disco, who died in 2012. As a singer, Donna Summer had many strings to her bow as this compilation shows. Including footage from her first performances on Top of the Pops with I Remember Yesterday and Winter Melody in 1977, to her last studio performance on Later with Jools Holland in 2004, as well as promo video of some key hits like I Feel Love and Enough is Enough.

programme.title: Disco: Soundtrack of a Revolution
programme.desc: In 1970s, in the aftermath of the Stonewall Riots, a sense of liberation fuelled a new sound from New York. In their quest for a safe space to meet – free from discrimination and violence – New York’s gay, black and minority ethnic communities started coming together in apartments and basement bars to dance. It was the beginning of a new kind of music and a pioneering dance floor culture that would sweep the world and change dance music forever.

programme.title: Black British Music at the BBC
programme.desc: DJ Spoony takes a musical journey that showcases the artists, songs and genres that have done so much to shape the nation’s musical landscape over the years – from old school right up to the present. Spoony has personally selected a playlist of 40 great tracks that bring together some of the most inspiring names from the worlds of pop, soul, ska, reggae, rap and garage - and finds the likes of Seal, The Selecter and Soul II Soul rubbing shoulders with FKA Twigs, Miss Dynamite and Dame Shirley Bassey. Spoony also celebrates the rich vein of collaboration that runs through so much Black British music, sharing songs and performances from acts, including Wretch 32 and Shola Ama, Loyle Carner and Jorja Smith, Little Simz and Cleo Sol, and Tinie Tempah and Labrinth.

programme.title: The Media Show
programme.desc: Six months after Péter Magyar's election ended Viktor Orbán's 16-year rule, Hungary's new government faces scrutiny over its promised press reforms. BBC East and Central Europe Correspondent Nick Thorpe reports from Budapest on how the country's media is changing. Broadcaster Anneka Rice reflects on fifty years since joining the BBC as a trainee, tracing her career across television and radio and the changes she has witnessed in British broadcasting. As the Cornell rape investigation continues, journalism experts including Dr Robert Topinka of Birkbeck, University of London, and Professor Kathleen Bartzen Culver of the University of Wisconsin-Madison consider the ethical and legal responsibilities of reporters covering sensitive cases.

programme.title: Stacey Dooley
programme.desc: Stacey Dooley looks into the deaths of women who have fallen from height, in cases where domestic abuse may have been part of the wider picture, and asks what role, if any, abuse can play in how these women die. As Stacey meets bereaved families, survivors, detectives, lawyers and campaigners, she explores how coercive control can shape women’s lives long before a fatal incident, and whether those histories are given sufficient weight when deaths are investigated. Among the cases, we see Stacey meet the family of Bianca Thomas, a young mother from Birmingham who died after falling from an 11th-floor balcony. Bianca's death was ruled accidental, but her family still have questions about the circumstances surrounding her death. Stacey also hears about the landmark case of Kimberley Milne, whose husband was convicted in Scotland of culpable homicide after sustained domestic abuse was found to have been a significant contributing factor in her death by suicide, and asks what that could mean for similar cases in England and Wales. Powerful and deeply personal, the programme explores grief, justice and the difficult questions surrounding women who die after falling from height.

programme.title: Horrible Histories
programme.desc: Some Vikings attack a monastery but cannot remember why; a peasant gets a posh makeover on Georgian Fashion Fix; Crimewatch BC tries to solve the murder of Julius Caesar; and the Egyptian Hieroglyphics song is guaranteed to leave you confused.

programme.title: Amanda & Alan's Italian Job
programme.desc: Amanda and Alan divide and conquer as they renovate the bathrooms. Amanda has big plans for converting one of the medieval tower rooms into a double height sumptuous en-suite complete with a Botticelli mural, roll-top bath and a gold resin floor, while Alan has the challenging task of transforming the small portaloo-sized bathroom into a minimalist wet room. Things don’t get off to the best of starts for Alan as he dismantles the old toilet, and Amanda’s dreams come crashing down as she discovers the ceiling she hoped to take down holds the tower together. To lift her spirits, Alan whisks Amanda away to the picturesque medieval town of San Gimignano, and the best friends get to grips with haggling at the oldest antiques market in Italy.

programme.title: Amanda & Alan's Italian Job
programme.desc: Amanda meets her match as she aims to turn the dark second bedroom into a country chic boudoir, inspired by the Tuscan sunrise. To help bring her vision to life, local friends Luca and Alessandro invite Amanda and Alan to visit their recently renovated 19th-century farmhouse, which motivates Amanda to brighten up the bedroom by borrowing light from the hallway. Keen to create a piece de resistance, Amanda ropes in Scott to build a bespoke headboard and takes her first steps into the world of upholstery, while Alan secretly signs up to a painting masterclass with local artist Tony to surprise Amanda with a showpiece of his own.

programme.title: Amanda & Alan's Italian Job
programme.desc: The DIY duo face their biggest renovation challenge yet, as Alan aims to transform the medieval tower room into a movie theatre inspired by Cinema Paradiso, while Amanda tries to turn the damp-ridden cellar carved out of the mountain’s rockface into a wine grotto. Hitting a brick wall with their ideas, Alan takes Amanda to the Guicciardini Strozzi Casona winery to meet descendants of Mona Lisa, princesses Irina and Natalia, for a tour of their ancient cellars and a tasting of their world-famous wines. Alan gets to work creating a bespoke seating area and ropes in Scott to give the entrance hall a much-needed makeover. Determined to make the most of her space, Amanda builds a path to access the cellar, but faces a hurdle when she discovers the rocky floor acts as a drain for water overflowing from the mountain. Local friend Warrie Price shakes off her renovation blues with some much-needed retail therapy in the medieval town of Pietrasanta.

programme.title: Amanda & Alan's Italian Job
programme.desc: Alan and Amanda are on the home stretch as they join forces to renovate the kitchen. Hoping to create the heart of their Italian home, the best friends aim to build an authentic rustic Tuscan design and set out repurposing the old chestnut beds from Amanda’s bedroom to form the kitchen units. Alan brushes up on his culinary skills, learning how to cook the classic Italian dish ravioli with local friend Luca, and Amanda brings a touch of colour to the kitchen, covering the fireplace in handmade tiles. Keen to source local Carrara marble for their worktops, the duo visit an active quarry in the Apuan Alps but face a treacherous journey to get there. For one last Tuscan treat, new friend Warrie invites Amanda and Alan for an afternoon of truffle hunting before they bid an emotional farewell with a party for the friends they’ve made over the summer.

programme.title: RuPaul's Drag Race UK
programme.desc: The search for the UK’s Next Drag Race Superstar continues. The queens’ over-acting skills are put to the test as they star in Ghost Hunties – a spooky, campy spoof of the UK’s favourite paranormal TV shows. Star of stage and screen, Slow Horses’ Kadiff Kirwan, swerves into the Drag Race lane as the extra special guest judge alongside Michelle Visage and Graham Norton while the queens once again fight for their survival.

programme.title: The Nice Guys
programme.desc: In 1970s Los Angeles, a mismatched pair of private eyes investigate a missing girl and the mysterious death of a porn star. Comedy starring Ryan Gosling and Russell Crowe.

programme.title: Man Like Mobeen
programme.desc: Mobeen and Nate are just weeks from the end of their sentence, but Mobeen’s work as one of the prison’s 'listeners' gets him into trouble with a terrifying inmate from another wing - a man known simply as Megalodon. Megalodon is determined to get a transfer to Mobeen’s wing so he can confront him about meddling in his business. Mobeen and Nate also have to deal with prison officer Saj, who is a constant thorn in their side. Alongside all this, Mobeen gets a visit from Aqsa, who is getting frustrated with certain aspects of life at medical school. Mobeen also pays a visit to the prison’s multifaith chaplain, who is a familiar figure, and another old face has a mission for Mobeen that could throw him back into a whole world of trouble - but will he take it on?

programme.title: Man Like Mobeen
programme.desc: Mobeen has landed himself in the prison infirmary, where he also has a mission – to befriend a man known as 'Memory Stick' and convince him to hand over vital information. In the infirmary, he also encounters a doctor, Nida, and there’s an instant spark between her and Mobeen. Nida also suggests she can help Aqsa with a placement for her medical degree, which she is thrilled with. Aqsa also receives some characteristically unhelpful advice from prison chaplain Uncle Shady. While Mobeen is in the hospital, Nate and Officer Harper develop a bromance that makes Mobeen jealous. Meanwhile, Megalodon is still trying to get transferred to Mobeen’s wing...

programme.title: BBC Comedy Short Films
programme.desc: Brothers Steve and Stu scramble to put on a last-minute birthday show for Steve’s daughter. If they fail, Steve’s in the doghouse and Stu might end up... dead.

programme.title: The Catch Up

programme.title: Horrible Histories
programme.desc: The Stuarts are confused by the newly discovered drink of tea, a Viking funeral ends in a massive fight, a child evacuated in the Blitz thinks farm animals are monsters, and some cowboys sing about life in the Wild West.

programme.title: Shrek the Third
programme.desc: Second sequel in the popular animated fantasy franchise. Newlyweds Shrek and Fiona face their first marital hurdle when the sudden death of King Harold means Shrek himself is next in line. However, with fatherhood looming, Shrek is reluctant. He decides to try and find the true heir - Fiona's errant, rebellious cousin. But while Shrek and his faithful companions Donkey and Puss in Boots go off in search of the heir, handsome rogue Prince Charming stages a coup at the castle. Featuring the voices of Mike Myers (Shrek), Eddie Murphy (Donkey), Cameron Diaz (Princess Fiona), Antonio Banderas (Puss in Boots), Julie Andrews (Queen Lillian), John Cleese (King Harold), Rupert Everett (Prince Charming), Eric Idle (Merlin), Justin Timberlake (Artie), John Krasinski (Lancelot), Ian McShane (Captain Hook) and Amy Poehler (Snow White).

programme.title: Death in Paradise
programme.desc: The play’s the thing! A touring theatre company are in town for their final performance of Shakespeare’s The Tempest on one of Saint Marie’s pristine beaches. During a raucous drinking scene, one of the leads keels over dead after drinking from a bottle of red wine. Tests reveal that the liquid contained a lethal quantity of cyanide. But two other actors drank from the same bottle both before and after the victim, and emerged unscathed. So how on earth did he, and only he, perish? Meanwhile, Mervin is informed that his half-brother Solomon is set to inherit everything from their deceased mother and promptly sell it off. Mervin is desperate to hold on to at least some sort of memento of her. The trouble is, Solomon will not return any of his calls. With time slipping away, Mervin may need to go to unexpected lengths to reach his brother.

programme.title: Mrs Brown's Boys
programme.desc: Lotto fever has hit Foley’s bar, and it doesn’t take long before rumours swirl around Finglas that Agnes is the jackpot winner. Meanwhile, a DNA test and the surprise return visit of Cathy’s childhood friend leaves Agnes with some serious questions to answer about her past. Guest-starring Debra Stephenson.

programme.title: Mrs Brown's Boys
programme.desc: Dermot and Maria decide to renew their wedding vows, forcing Agnes to organise the ceremony alongside arch-nemesis Hillary. Will she be able to cope with Hillary’s high-society demands? Meanwhile, Fathers Damien and Trevor go on a mountain pilgrimage that goes wrong. Will they make it back in time to officiate at the ceremony? Or at all?

programme.title: Mrs Brown's Boys
programme.desc: Mrs Brown becomes a podcast sensation – without even leaving the house. Cathy is horrified to discover her mother has accidentally hijacked her new podcast project. Guest-starring Simon Delaney.

programme.title: Alan Partridge: Alpha Papa
programme.desc: To save his own job, Alan gets radio colleague Pat laid off, but when the man returns to the relaunched station with a shotgun and a siege ensues, Alan is given the high-profile role of go-between, trying to appease both the hostage taker and armed police. So lots of people have Alan in their sights. Hit big screen spin-off for the self-obsessed former TV 'personality', from BBC Films.

programme.title: Ice Road Truckers
programme.desc: Lisa, Scooter and company driver Muskie Todd team up as a three-truck convoy to take on the notorious Asheweig Road. The trio must work together to survive a looming disaster. Meanwhile, across the wilderness, IRT veteran Todd Dewey takes on a route he has never seen before, forcing him out of his truck and into a fight against the elements.

programme.title: The Celebrity Traitors
programme.desc: As the players go deeper into the game, a new day brings new suspicions amongst the Faithful. The mission forces the celebrities to work in teams under terrifying conditions, and with the murdering hour approaching, the players take their seats at the Round Table. Will the Faithful work as a team to uncover a Traitor?

programme.title: The Celebrity Traitors: Uncloaked
programme.desc: Ed chats to any banished and murdered players from episode 4. Find out their reactions as they discover the Traitors' identities. Former players dissect all the latest castle action and game playing.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: With two children, a menagerie of animals and plans for even more, Cheryl and Barry are swapping Somerset suburbia for the wide-open spaces of Moray and Aberdeenshire. Steve Brown is working with a £425,000 budget to find them a family home where land is every bit as important as the house itself. Steve also visits a local football club scoring some impressive green goals, using new technologies while remaining at the heart of its community.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents this quiz show where a team of four friends Karen, Andrew, Mary and Arwel take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: The Reluctant Vampire
programme.desc: Val has to come up with a plan to pass the vampire initiation ceremony despite his huge secret. However, his curiosity about human life gets the better of him, and he sneaks to the village, where he bumps into Gertie and is thrust straight into human family life. His two worlds collide when he’s invited to a party.

programme.title: Weatherman Walking
programme.desc: Derek explores what lies beneath his feet when he revisits the Great Orme, the Offa’s Dyke Path and the last surviving cast iron footbridge in Merthyr Tydfil.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Politics Live
programme.desc: The big political issues of the day.

programme.title: Impossible
programme.desc: Game show presented by Rick Edwards in which players score points by answering questions correctly. However, they must avoid the Impossible answers, otherwise they will be eliminated from the show until the next day. In each episode, there are three rounds, and the three highest scorers from each round play against each other in the final. The winner of this battle faces a £10,000 question.

programme.title: The Answer Run
programme.desc: Comedian Jason Manford hosts an exciting, fast-paced quiz show, where three couples face a series of 50/50 questions which hurtle The Answer Run down towards them. Across three rounds, the couples build up their cash pots, but only one pair can face The Final Run and win the chance to take home their cash prize. Who will swipe their way to victory?

programme.title: The Boss
programme.desc: Susan Calman hosts the quiz show of tactics, knowledge and nerve. Contestants must work as a team, but ultimately there can only be one Boss. Who will pick off their opponents and walk away with the thousands of pounds on offer?

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo’s railway journey through Cumbria and Dumfriesshire heads to the hills as he follows in the footsteps of the Lakeland poets. In Keswick, he retraces the adventurous walks of Samuel Taylor Coleridge, discovering how one of his legendary routes has been used as a form of therapy. Michael visits the striking ruins of Lowther Castle - once a grand gothic estate, now reborn as an extraordinary garden. With 18 million visitors a year, the Lake District National Park is challenged with balancing tourism and conservation. Michael joins a local litter-picking group who want to educate visitors. At Ullswater, he discovers the native Herdwick and Rough Fell sheep, whose wool is finding eco-friendly uses today, and tries his hand at herding the flock with dependable sheepdog Pick.

programme.title: The Great House Revival
programme.desc: Siobhan, her partner Timmie and their two young children hope to bring new life to their small village in Ireland by renovating the old post office to become their forever home. But with funds running low and work grinding to a halt, will their dream family home become a reality?

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel and the team visit Witley Court in Worcestershire where they discover more intriguing finds, including the complete cast of an early puppet theatre discovered in a loft, a Worcester plate made as a royal gift, a drawing by LS Lowry and an extremely rare piece of early Staffordshire slipware, similar to the famous Ozzie the Owl, and valued even more highly.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Flog It! comes from the the Discovery Museum, home to a fantastic collection of science and social history. It is the first science museum outside London and located in the centre of Newcastle upon Tyne. Paul Martin is joined by experts Anita Manning and Nick Davies. Members of the public arrive at the museum laden with hundreds of antiques and collectibles to be valued by the Flog It! experts. Later in the show, a number of items are sold at auction. Paul finds out about the famous Northumbrian landscape gardener Capability Brown.

programme.title: House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Chizzy Akudolu, Stephen Bailey, Banjo Beale and Philippa Dunne take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, Michael Sheen. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted with the brand new House of Games record player?

programme.title: Strictly - It Takes Two
programme.desc: Ellie Taylor has training room exclusives that reveal how some of the celebs are getting on with their next dances. Also, a panel of Strictly pros pop by to reveal some dance secrets.

programme.title: Celebrity Antiques Road Trip
programme.desc: Used to life spent on the road, touring stand-up comedians Lloyd Griffith and Rhys James are off on a road trip around Wales and south west England. They venture through the valleys in a jazzy Jaguar E-Type, accompanied by jewellery pro Hettie Jago and coin specialist Tim Medhurst. The foursome are off in search of amazing antiques and perfect punchlines. In Pontypool, Rhys makes an unusual find in the form of a picture frame-cum-radio, but is it in with a shot at auction? Meanwhile, in Monmouth, Lloyd uncovers a quirky sporting scoreboard he hopes can lead him to victory. In a break from antiques hunting, the pair head behind the scenes at Bristol Zoo Project. But when the visit turns mucky, which of our two comedians will have the last laugh?

programme.title: Secrets & Spies: A Nuclear Game
programme.desc: With Gordievsky’s help, Britain identifies Mikhail Gorbachev as a possible new contender for Soviet leader; he could be the ticket to better relations between east and west. But fragile steps towards diplomacy are threatened by the vested interests of other spies still stuck in the old-world order. The CIA is set on knowing who Britain’s super spy is, but their head of Soviet counterintelligence, Aldrich Ames, is getting disillusioned. He turns traitor for a paltry sum, and shortly afterwards, Gordievsky is summoned back to Russia to almost certain danger. The episode includes exclusive audio recordings of Aldrich Ames, audio interviews from Oleg Gordievsky, interviews with former KGB, FBI, CIA and MI6 officers, some of whom have never spoken before, as well as colleagues of Thatcher and Reagan.

programme.title: The Book That Changed My Life
programme.desc: Inspired by her passion to get people reading, Her Majesty Queen Camilla joins four remarkable people to share the stories of books that shaped them. Warm, emotional and full of hope, the film shows how reading can lift people up, open minds and even change lives in a celebration of the magic power inside every book.

programme.title: Live at the Apollo
programme.desc: Iain Stirling introduces comedians Harriet Dyer and Maria Shehata to the stage.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the news stories of the day. With Paddy O'Connell.

programme.title: Unspun World with John Simpson
programme.desc: Unspun World provides an unvarnished version of the week's major global news stories - reliable, honest and essential viewing. The BBC's world affairs editor, John Simpson, brings his experience and expertise to bear on the most important international stories. In discussion with the BBC's unparalleled range of experts across the world, he uses their unique local knowledge to go beyond the headlines to get to the unspun truth about the world.

programme.title: John Simpson - 60 Years at the BBC
programme.desc: John Simpson looks back at his extraordinary 60-year career at the BBC - reporting on the biggest global stories of the era. In a frank, personal and revealing documentary, he reflects on the changing world he has witnessed: the revolution in Iran that seemed destined to fail, his brutal kidnapping in Beirut, the fall of the Berlin Wall, two wars in Iraq, the invasion of Afghanistan and a mind-altering trip up the Amazon. From the Broadcasting House newsroom in 1966 to World Affairs editor, he looks back at memorable encounters with inspiring leaders and cruel dictators - the figures who have shaped history, including Nelson Mandela, Margaret Thatcher, Saddam Hussein, Colonel Gaddafi and Volodymyr Zelensky. The programme also features his insights into the role of the BBC today and the challenges faced in the age of fake news.

programme.title: Finding Britain’s Slave Traders with David Olusoga
programme.desc: David Olusoga meets the historians who have built the Register of British Slave Traders. For five years, they have searched through thousands of documents, piecing together a comprehensive picture of over 13,000 individuals who were investors in the slave trade. Anyone can now log on and discover who the slave traders were, where they lived, how much money they made and the links between modern British institutions and the trade in human beings. David discovers how the monarchy drove the early British slave trade. He learns how Elizabeth I and the early Stuarts gave their support to early slavery ventures; how the restored monarchy in the 1660s, seeking new ways to strengthen its finances and authorities, chartered a joint-stock monopoly company dedicated to the trade in enslaved Africans; and how James II, the company's governor, becoming king led to the emergence of a new and rival set of companies and investors who would transform the slave trade.

programme.title: Eva Longoria: Searching for France
programme.desc: Avant-garde Paris is steeped in the traditions of haute cuisine, dating back to Louis XIV's refinement of dining conventions with his ‘art of the table’ at the court of Versailles. At Alain Ducasse’s Le Meurice, Eva eats a single oyster dressed in rhubarb in a flamboyant display reminiscent of the Sun King’s food theatre. And she meets the young chefs leading a new food scene which blends French technique with global influences, including Mory Sacko at MoSuke and Hanz Gueco at Le Cheval d’Or.

programme.title: Time
programme.desc: New chaplain Marie-Louise arrives at the young offender institution HMYOI Alderwick and finds herself immediately at odds with traditionalist and world-weary custodial manager Bailey, who is dealing with his own personal crisis. They lock horns over how to handle Christopher, a young man with a stammer who has recently reconnected with his birth mother. Meanwhile, Peter and his friends arrive at the prison after being involved in an attack on a man, and James is relocated from another prison.

programme.desc: Chris and Flo head to Oxford to help Cat and Nic transform their long, featureless garden into a Brighton-inspired family retreat.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: Autumn is in full swing at Longmeadow, and Monty is making the most of the season. As he prunes roses, stores the apple harvest and plants out spring cabbages in the kitchen garden, he also turns his attention to next year, sharing ideas for bulbs that will bring colour and life to a shady border. Rachel de Thame visits a specialist wildflower nursery to discover how these beautiful plants can transform our gardens while providing a vital lifeline for wildlife. In Devon, Toby Buckland is back with more ingenious horticultural hacks designed to make gardening easier, cheaper and more enjoyable. A couple in Shropshire reveal the artistry and dedication behind their remarkable topiary creations, while an Oxfordshire gardener proves that the season is far from over with a dazzling display of late autumn colour.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo’s railway journey through Cumbria and Dumfriesshire takes him to the rolling countryside around Aspatria to meet a couple who swapped their old life for organic dairy farming. Embracing regenerative principles, they’ve traded quantity for quality - alongside their beloved cow named Taylor Swift. At a hi-tech creamery, Michael discovers how their sustainable milk becomes cheddar cheese for supermarkets nationwide. Arriving at the historic railway hub of Carlisle, Michael discovers a vast Roman structure. His journey ends in the imposing borderlands fortress of Carlisle Castle, where intriguing 15th-century graffiti offers a glimpse into the minds of medieval soldiers.

programme.title: The Great House Revival
programme.desc: Entrepreneur Aoibheann has found the ideal location to retreat from her busy life in Galway - a modest derelict cottage in the heart of the Burren. But Aoibheann’s creativity and plans for the cottage know no bounds, and if she can't rein in some of her ideas, will this renovation ever progress?

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel and the team head for the Magna Centre in Rotherham. Among the items brought to light are a rare clock given as a gift by Queen Victoria, a stash of silver valued at over £5,000 and a treasured set of Beatles memorabilia.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Roll up, roll up, this edition of Flog It! comes from the historic Blackpool Tower Circus. Paul Martin is joined by experts Anita Manning and James Lewis. Together the team pick out a selection of antiques and collectables to be sold at auction. James discovers a scary-looking tribal mask from Africa, and Anita finds a Flog It! favourite: a Clarice Cliff tea set. But will a Doulton figure bought at a car boot sale cause a surprise at the sale room? Paul also takes a look at the spooky side of Lancashire when he investigates the story of the Pendle witch trial.

programme.title: House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Chizzy Akudolu, Stephen Bailey, Banjo Beale and Philippa Dunne take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, Michael Sheen. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted with the brand new House of Games record player?

programme.title: Strictly - It Takes Two
programme.desc: Ellie Taylor serves up more backstage gossip from the world of Strictly. Vicky Gill showcases what some of the couples are wearing at the weekend, and Strictly host Emma Willis drops in for a chat.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: A health-conscious couple from London enlist Sonali Shah to help them spend £1.3 million on a detached property in Surrey with enough land to create a wellness retreat. Taking a breather from house-hunting, Sonali immerses herself in the county’s ancient woodlands as she learns about the Japanese practice of forest bathing.

programme.title: Monty Don’s British Gardens
programme.desc: Monty travels across some of the country’s most stunning landscapes, heading across the north of England to Northern Ireland. Here, Monty sees the ingenuity, passion and determination of British people to garden and create gardens, no matter what the canvas.

programme.title: Surgeons: At the Edge of Life
programme.desc: Operations to transform patients’ lives. Surgeons at Addenbrooke’s and Royal Papworth take on a high-risk spine procedure and perform open-heart surgery on an 80-year-old patient.

programme.title: Inside No. 9
programme.desc: Helen and her teenage son Zach don’t really get on, until a random act of kindness brings the mysterious Bob to their front door. He seems to understand their problems and offers to help. But what effect will spending time with this kindly stranger have on their lives?

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the crucial news stories of the day. With Katie Razzall.

programme.title: Uncanny
programme.desc: Danny is joined by Sybil, the manager of a charity shop in the home counties. From the day she opened, Sybil felt a strange presence, which only heightened when other workers also said they sensed someone in the shop with them. As time went on and more workers had the same experience, activity began to ramp up. Things started to move in front of multiple witnesses, and when building work was done on the shop, the presence finally revealed itself - to terrifying effect. After the discovery of a hidden room, clues as to who this presence could be come to light. Danny does some digging into the building’s past and finds some extraordinary leads as to who could be responsible, while also exploring the phenomenon of stone tape theory, where past events are somehow recorded in the fabric of buildings. As ever, the audience is invited to share their theories and help crack the case.

programme.title: Blue Lights

programme.title: The Devil’s Confession: The Lost Eichmann Tapes
programme.desc: Escaping from postwar Europe, Nazi criminal Adolf Eichmann establishes a new life in Argentina, where he meets fellow Nazi Willem Sassen. Together, they record a comprehensive account of his career. The tapes disappear when Eichmann is captured and taken to stand trial in Jerusalem, but excerpts of his interview surface in Life Magazine, and Israeli prosecutor Gideon Hausner is determined to use Eichmann’s recorded confession as evidence during the trial.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Flo and Sue are in Stevenage to help mother and daughter Margaret and Elizabeth transform their south-facing garden. While blessed with sunlight, the space is currently a chaotic jumble of mismatched plant pots, overgrown bushes and uneven, sloped steps, making it overwhelming and difficult to enjoy. Their dream is to turn it into a mother–daughter retreat with a serene, shaded relaxation garden. Elizabeth and Margaret envision a charming pergola draped in delicate vines, offering a peaceful spot to unwind together. Wider, gently sloping steps and accessible raised beds will allow Margaret to continue her beloved gardening safely, while lush, in-ground plants reduce maintenance. They also hope for privacy screening and planting that discreetly hides the shed at the back of the garden. Elizabeth juggles a demanding full-time job with caring for her ageing mother, leaving little time to work on the garden. Margaret is retired and longing to enjoy the outdoors, but her partial sight makes the current low-lying plants and treacherous steps a real obstacle to relaxation and upkeep. Can the team turn this challenging plot into a peaceful mother–daughter retreat on a £4,500 budget?

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents this quiz show where a team of four friends, Louise, Mark, Suzy and Rich, take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Wilderness with Simon Reeve
programme.desc: Simon Reeve journeys deep into Canada’s vast and empty Yukon territory – one of North America’s most iconic and remote landscapes. Covering an area almost the size of Spain but home to fewer than 50,000 people, the Yukon is a land of immense forests, glaciers, rivers and wildlife. In wealthy, modern Canada, Simon wants to find out how the people and the wildlife of this immense wilderness are faring - all while searching for an apex predator, the grizzly bear.

At his mausoleum, he reflects on Burns’s enduring legacy before enjoying one of his songs performed in the Scots language. Further north into the Lowther Hills, Michael strikes gold in the rich geological landscape around Wanlockhead, Scotland’s highest village, and rides a charming heritage industrial railway across the stunning terrain. The journey ends at the spectacular Palladian mansion of Dumfries House, home to a world-class Chippendale furniture collection and the headquarters of the King’s Foundation. In a traditional skills workshop, Michael discovers why he was never destined to be a builder.
